observation_summary: The Dfp.multiply(int x) method failed for integer inputs outside the range [0, RADIX), causing incorrect results (NaN) because it only supported a limited range of inputs.
reasoning_summary: The fix implements a conditional check to handle the general case for integer multiplication. When the input is within the fast-path range [0, RADIX), it uses the existing multiplyFast(x) method. For all other integers, it now correctly delegates to the general multiply(Dfp) method by converting the integer to a Dfp instance. This is a correction to the procedure/method implementation to satisfy the contract of the FieldElement interface.
evidence_used: The bug report states that Dfp.multiply(int x) was limited to 0 <= n <= 9999, violating the FieldElement.multiply(int n) contract.
The fix diff shows the addition of an if-else block that delegates to multiply(newInstance(x)) when the input is outside the fast-path range.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a conditional check, the primary purpose is to extend the functionality of the method to support the full range of integers, which is an algorithmic/methodological correction rather than just a validation check.
